correctness.rationale: For every convex polygon with noncollinear positive-length sides, all ordered edge choices are partitioned into same-edge, adjacent-edge, and nonadjacent-edge pairs. Same-edge parameter areas give \(2Pr-mr^2\). The adjacent-edge difference map has Jacobian \(\sin\alpha\) and an image sector of aperture \(\theta=\pi-\alpha\), giving \(\theta r^2/(2\sin\theta)\) per ordered pair; finite sides do not truncate for suitably small radius. Nonadjacent edges are uniformly separated. The exact equality follows, not just asymptotics. Euler sine-product positivity proves \(f(t)-t^2/6\) strictly convex for \(0<t<\pi\), Jensen gives the variance remainder, and an actual convex centrally symmetric even-sided polygon family gives limiting ratio \(1/6\). The code performs distinct finite checks without replacing analytic arguments.

evidence: In the published fourth-coefficient proof, the area-covariogram method integrates two interior-area points, with \(C_4(Q)=(8\pi^2)^{-1}\sum_i[1+(\pi-\alpha_i)\cot(\alpha_i)]\).
Here ordered arclength pairs on adjacent edges map by determinant \(\sin\alpha\), yielding \(B(Q)=\sum_i[(\pi-\alpha_i)/\sin\alpha_i-1]\) and a second-order corner contribution.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A consequence of the prior interior law would need a theorem transferring 2D area sampling to the 1D normalized perimeter product distribution, and no such statement appears in the inspected result; the polynomial order, measures, coefficient functions, and best stability constants differ. The prior regular polygon chord law cannot imply the arbitrary-polygon equiangular equality classification or the globally optimal 1/6 variance coefficient. The claim is not labeled first-ever independently.

value.rationale: This is a natural geometric-probability measurement: the distribution of exceptionally short chords joining independent boundary locations. It yields an exact polygon-dependent law whose correction is a pure corner-angle invariant, a sharp bound among all equal-side-count angle patterns, a full equality classification for equiangular shapes, and a universal best quantitative angular-rigidity constant. The degree and coefficient differ fundamentally from interior-point sampling, offering a direct angular diagnostic from a perimeter probability law. It does not claim polygon reconstruction or a general-distance algorithm.
